comments.comment: I’m struggling to find the words. And you’ve said this perfectly. ❤️ sharing . Sending love and a hug.

Exactly. There are also children who are “perfect” and end up with a childhood/teen/adult diagnosis later one that can be devastating. Those people still had a chance to live and receive a miracle regardless. Every life is precious. Every. Single. Life ✝️

We were also told our daughter had Down syndrome after she was born (we would of never terminated it would of been nice to know but It was a very tough and emotional moment for our family, and there were a lot of unknowns in those first days. Looking back, though, I wouldn't trade her for anything in the world. She has brought so much joy, love, and perspective to our lives and is truly one of the best things that has ever happened to our family. 4 months in hospital then open heart surgery she is thriving so blessed 💙💛✨

I’m to the point the where I think you need your own morning tv show.

You’re so thoughtful in your conversations.

Smart and fun to watch.

I saw that post and my heart broke.
I couldn't have said it better 👏 👏👏

They probably should have kept this to themselves. Very personal decision and everyone has different viewpoints on it. Unfortunately, if they didn’t think they could handle it, it was probably the right decision for them!
I would have adopted the baby but only if it was Down my little guy is now 12 nothing to be afraid of just happiness and joy for the last 12 years
Agree 👏 it’s very concerning. It’s shocking to see some of the comments on this. I really feel the medical community need to be better educated on Down syndrome
But why do you only get a test result at 5 months? I got mine at 11/12 weeks! And then you can have it removed because it's still early.
connect them with adoptive parents that would love their child!!!!!!!
